assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read in full with its front matter: the canonical KSOA-G1 character monograph series/kamakura-sho/studies/KSOA_MOTOYA_KITSUKAWA.md and the canonical directed partnership study series/kamakura-sho/studies/KSOA_PARTNERSHIP.md. Both are repository literary analysis of the seven Japanese publisher novels (文春文庫) through V07 EPI p[0151] and KSOA-V07-H-0015. The ledgers, deep readings, claim-revision entries and the project's reconstruction specification and readiness audit that these studies link are not curated on this subject; the ledger and reading locators cited below are quoted from the two studies as their own citations, and no claim rests on unread linked material. No primary-source inspection was performed.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Motoya Kitsukawa from V01 (rank pride, independent questions about Ashina's health and the Torii article connection) through V02 workplace verification, apology support and accepted off-duty request, V03 economic reading, evidence presentation and identified-officer stay, V04 complementary footage proposal and requested questioning lead, V05 off-duty craft interview, self-recognized attraction and arrest, V06 Mizutani omission, Kosugi and taxi alibi limits, deferral recommendation, Emiri omission and family narrative, to V07 authorized-release boundary, concealed private meeting, photograph recognition, smaller self-judgment and the private pledge at EPI p[0135]-p[0151] as endpoint. Capability states split at located changes: before V05 his attraction to Emiri is absent; within V07 his reading of Emiri's affection holds until the epilogue discloses her private relation to Izumida (EPI p[0087]-p[0143]), and his resolve to support Asumi is formed only at the finale and is not known to Asumi. Whether he discloses or acts on the pledge is outside the seven novels.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives an explicit interpretation: he notices when a proposed explanation outruns the evidence while making similarly hopeful leaps about people he likes; his firmer work takes concrete forms (locating a record, a follow-up question, marking what can be said publicly); and a gap separates visible competence from self-appraisal. It predicts a characteristic error: accommodating acceptance of a liked person's account (V06 Emiri distance from Nonaka; V06 Yakushiji's candor; V07 projection corrected by the epilogue), while his evidence standard holds (V07 authorized release, refusing a fan's assurance, asking for a corroborator). Not B: the studies list contributing factors for off-duty help (childhood obligation, being identified, local civilians, Asumi's appeals, resentment) without saying which decides, and present the V06 deferral and omission as acts with different bases without resolving the motive; that is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. The witness-evaluation domain is B-like, but this whole-subject record does not establish a discriminating account elsewhere. Not D: an explicit, located account with a predicted error type supports narrow extrapolation.

The partnership table gives a directed state for each volume V01-V07, and the monograph traces a development from bruised rank pride (V01) to defined contributions (V02-V06) to a smaller self-judgment despite praise and a changed description of his future role (V07). Not B: apart from the V07 finale, the changes are not causally sequenced or located as state transitions. Not D: per-volume states and the endpoint are explicit.

The monograph states that his speech tracks audience: formal identification at the first scene, rank used as a mock honorific with Asumi, 俺 and surname address in ordinary talk with her, 吉川です in V07 official introduction, 僕 with Nagasaka, and courteous and more familiar turns in the private meeting; it distinguishes narrated hesitation from the calm phrasing others hear. Not B: few utterances are quoted and no sentence-level rule is given. Not D: address and self-reference are analyzed across audiences and functions.

The monograph records preferences beyond case work: familiar food when tired (V06 C01 p[0870]-p[0899]), a newly acquired taste and attention to Izumida's competence at the V07 counter, and a family narrative explaining why salaried work feels more secure (V06 C02 p[0509]-p[0515]). Not C: these are located in two volumes without a conditional account of ordinary choices. Not E: they are distributed and tied to explained background.

The partnership table gives directed, located states toward Asumi for every volume, and the studies separately analyze Emiri (attraction affecting evaluation, V05; omitted connection, V06; misread affection, V07), Sayaka (interview modeling ordinary questions, V05; qualified fact under challenge, V06), Yakushiji and Nagasaka. Address changes are read as changes of function, not steady escalation. Not B: the studies do not say which conditions decide whether he helps Asumi off duty or how far he resists her lead. Not D: the deltas are directed and located.

As primary focalizer, his inner states are narrated in every volume and the studies analyze their relation to speech and action: injured pride that hears an invitation as condescension (V01), resentment that does not undo help (V02, V05), private concern about witness pressure (V03), inward qualification of Asumi's account and withdrawal from the quarrel (V06), mock deference that protests inwardly, recognition that attraction may bias him (V05), a smaller self-judgment despite praise and the unheard pledge (V07). Not A: two short studies, no catalogue of inner voice and no test of predictions. Not C: interior access is direct and repeated rather than inferred from action.

Interpersonal conflict is located and interpreted: declining Asumi's emotional overture (V02), withdrawing from the V06 bar quarrel, reporting sensitive information despite anticipated friction (V06), keeping the V07 meeting from Asumi because he anticipates conflict, and challenging the line from grievance to action (V07). Not B: the studies do not explain why he reports in V06 but conceals in V07 beyond noting the acts have different consequences, and physical confrontation (the V05 arrest) is not analyzed. Not D: an avoidance tendency and its countercase are located.

Because he is focalized, part of his weighing is represented: private questioning of pressure on witnesses (V03), keeping his name out of the piece (V05), a qualified fact under Sayaka's challenge and Yakushiji's possible responsibility treated as a distinct post-event matter (V06), and the V07 limit to the authorized release with a corroborator required. Not B: his private decision whether to report the V07 meeting and the V06 omission are not explained by a stated rule. Not D: located judgments with reasons are analyzed.

Humor appears only locally: rank used as a mock honorific with Asumi and his inward protest under it. No humorous conduct is analyzed beyond that. Not D: there is no distributed body of humorous conduct.

Both items cover V01-V07, a complete series, with located contributions in every volume and the endpoint V07 EPI p[0151]. Not B: two short studies (about 20 KB) are the whole curated set, with no operational model, ledger entries or probe curated on this subject. Not D: every volume has located analysis.

Affirmative located limits: his V07 projection about Emiri fails when the epilogue discloses her reason (cited to V07 CL-0005-R01); his favorable reading of Yakushiji is vulnerable to Asumi's performance hypothesis (V06); the pledge is internal and Asumi cannot hear it; it follows earlier support and is not the first instance of care; outsider labels and his action have distinct sources (V02); the romantic reading has limited authority. Not B: few limits and none tested. Not D: each is located.

Claims carry volume anchors, several page anchors (V06 C01-C02, V07 C01, C03-C04 and EPI), an explicit endpoint at V07 EPI p[0151], the epilogue split of his knowledge about Emiri, and the rule that the pledge's disclosure lies outside the novels. Not B: no knowledge views are given for earlier states. Not D: the endpoint and the within-volume split are explicit.

conditions: Use is illustrative reconstruction of a named V01-V07 state, never attributed quotation; Japanese lines presented as canon are retrieved from the witnesses.

Self-reference and address follow the sampled audiences: 俺 and surname with Asumi, mock rank title in deference-protest, 吉川です in official introduction, 僕 with Nagasaka; unsampled audiences are lower confidence.
Narrated hesitation is inner response; spoken lines heard by others are calmer, and an inner pledge or judgment is not voiced unless the scenario states it.
scenario_readiness.note: The audience-dependent address and self-reference analysis and the inner/outer distinction constrain short exchanges enough for illustrative use. Not READY: few utterances are quoted and no sentence-level rule is given. Not NOT_READY: the sampled audiences and functions are analyzed.

conditions: Change one fact of a case, witness relationship or assignment at a time from a named state, and state it.
Predict an evidence-bounded answer on authorized information but a more accommodating reading of a witness he likes; mark off-duty help and disclosure to Asumi as low confidence.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named V01-V07 state, with the V07 pre-epilogue and post-epilogue knowledge about Emiri kept apart; the V07 pledge exists only from the finale.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Asumi as his senior partner and childhood acquaintance, a civilian witness or expert, a superior, or Sayaka as an off-duty acquaintance and journalist.
setting_constraints: A comparable Japanese prefectural police investigation in a local community, with his rank as 巡査長 under a senior partner.
No cross-series settings or changed institutional roles without a stated assumption.

scenario_readiness.note: His concrete contributions, evidence standard and accommodating error are located and repeated, which supports bounded counterfactuals inside comparable investigative work. Not READY: what decides off-duty help and concealment is unresolved. Not NOT_READY: the contribution and error patterns recur across volumes.

conditions: Limited to off-duty or work-adjacent scenes with Asumi, Sayaka or known local figures (meals, counters, invited help), using the located preferences and resentment-with-help pattern.
Family, romantic and unfamiliar social settings beyond the V06 family narrative require abstention.
scenario_readiness.note: Off-duty scenes, food preferences and family background support narrow situated interpretation. Not READY: ordinary choices have no conditional account. Not NOT_READY: several off-duty and counter scenes are analyzed.

conditions: Decisions about what case information to release, how to question a witness and whether an account needs corroboration, at a named state.
Whether he reports a private contact to Asumi or omits a liked witness's connection is not predicted beyond the sampled V06 and V07 cases.
scenario_readiness.note: His information-release and witness-handling judgments are represented with reasons. Not READY: his private reporting decisions are not explained by a rule. Not NOT_READY: located reasoning exists, unlike for his partner.

The partnership study gives the romantic reading limited authority and leaves the development of their reliance outside work open, his V07 reading of Emiri's affection is a corrected misreading, and the pledge's disclosure lies outside the novels. Not CONDITIONAL: the evidence affirmatively withholds a romantic trajectory rather than being silent.

conditions: Record checks, concrete follow-up questions, footage or alibi verification, evidence presentation and public-statement limits as a 巡査長 working with Asumi, at a named state.
Initiative is not fixed: he can propose and lead (V04) or follow a strong lead while challenging its links (V07); state the assignment and rank context.
scenario_readiness.note: Located investigative contributions in every volume support bounded professional reconstruction. Not READY: his initiative relative to Asumi and his reporting choices vary without a stated rule. Not NOT_READY: the contribution forms recur.

known_limits.statement: He accepts liked people's accounts too readily: Emiri's distance from Nonaka (V06), Yakushiji's candor (V06) and his V07 projection, which the epilogue corrects.

Personal hope does not move his evidence standard on authorized information: in V07 he limits his answer to the authorized release, does not let a fan's assurance exclude a witness and asks for a corroborator.
The V07 resolve to support Asumi is internal; Asumi cannot hear it, it is not the first instance of his care, and whether he discloses or acts on it is outside the seven novels.
A romantic reading of the partnership has limited authority; the best-supported ending is professional and interpersonal reliance with its development outside work left open.
The studies do not say which conditions decide his off-duty help or his choice between reporting (V06) and concealing (V07) private contacts.
The curated set is two short literary studies; no operational model, validation probe or ledger entries are curated on this subject.
